20.0.s.en: (1) David tells Jonathan frankly what is in Saul's heart

20.0.0.en: Although David had seen Saul among the prophets praising and glorifying God, he was not reassured about him and preferred to flee, because he knew what was in Saul's heart. So he went down from Naioth, near Ramah, to Ramah, where he met Jonathan, and he opened his heart to him and asked him in protest, What have I done to your father, and why is he angry with me, and what is my crime for which he seeks my death?!

20.1.0.en: Jonathan, the loving one, answered, also in protest, that this would never happen, and to reassure David's heart he told him that his father Saul told him all his affairs and thoughts, however small, so if he wanted to kill him he would surely tell him.

20.2.0.en: As the Lord lives and as your soul lives: an expression of an oath for emphasis.

20.2.1.en: David confirmed his words to Jonathan with an oath so that he would believe him, that his father was determined to kill him and that only one step separated him from death. But Saul also knew the extent of Jonathan's love and friendship for David, and therefore he decided to hide this particular matter from him so that his heart would not grieve, and also so that he would not prevent him from killing David.

20.3.0.en: Jonathan wanted to express his love and loyalty to David and also to reassure his heart, so he said to him, Whatever you ask of me, I will do it, and I promise you this.

20.4.0.en: When Jonathan told David that he would carry out everything David asked of him, "David" indeed began to ask Jonathan to help him in his plan. The Jews celebrated the new moons as spiritual feasts (Num 28:11-15), offering sacrifices and making feasts, and of course the king prepared a monthly feast from which all his commanders and men ate, David among them. So David asked Jonathan to hide for three days in one of the fields and not to attend his father's feast.

20.5.0.en: If the king asked about David and his empty place, Jonathan was to answer that he had permitted him to go to his father's house in the village of Bethlehem to offer with his family the sacrifice that his people were accustomed to offer every year; and indeed it was among the customs of the Jewish clans to offer memorial offerings at the new moons.

20.6.0.en: If your father's answer is agreement and approval, this will be a sign of peace and that he does not harbor evil against me; but if he becomes agitated and angry and his wrath grows fierce, know that your father intended evil against me, that is, my death.

20.7.0.en: You have brought your servant into a covenant with you: David's thanks for the humility of Jonathan, the king's son, and his entering into a covenant with his servant David; and this is also humility on David's part, because he forgot that he was the king and remembered only that he was Jonathan's servant. In this, Jonathan, you will have done me a great kindness, since you will have saved innocent blood from your father's hand, especially as you are my friend and the Lord is witness to the covenant of our friendship. But if you see me as guilty or deserving of death, then kill me yourself rather than hand me over to your father.

20.8.0.en: Again Jonathan answers David, saying, "Far be it from you," which means that I forbid you to say this about yourself, that you are a doer of evil. But my friend, do you think that if I knew that a danger threatened you from my father, I would hide it from you?!?.! That is, he reassured him that he would not die.

20.8.1.en: If you sense evil in some place, or a sin into which you will fall if you go to that place or meet certain people, flee and keep away so that you do not fall into sin; this is wisdom and strength, not weakness, for what matters is that you keep yourself in purity and peace.

20.9.0.en: David asked Jonathan again, But who will tell me and inform me if Saul's answer carries evil? But before Jonathan answered him with anything, he asked him to go out together outside the city to the field, meaning to an empty place.

20.10.0.en: O Lord God of Israel: an oath in the form of a prayer.

20.10.1.en: Jonathan began his words to David by addressing God, that is, to call God as witness to the truth of his words in order to reassure David, which is a style resembling an oath. The content of the words was that tomorrow, during the king's feast at the new moon, if he learned that Saul loved David and wished him good, he would tell him so; but if he did not tell him, may God do to Jonathan every evil, "may He do so and more also". But if he sensed that his father was harboring evil toward him and truly wanted to kill him, he would also tell him and let him flee from his presence. He prayed that the Lord would be with David and give him victory, as He had been with his father in the early days and gave him victory over his enemies.

20.11.0.en: After Jonathan pledged to tell David what was in Saul's heart and promised to help him flee in the case of his father's anger, he now asks a covenant from his friend "David": that when God gives him the kingdom and he becomes a man of influence, he should not only spare Jonathan and promise not to kill him, but should also care for all of Jonathan's offspring and house, in the event that he alone holds power after God has destroyed all his enemies.

20.12.0.en: Let the Lord require it: it means, let the Lord take vengeance.

20.12.1.en: Jonathan repeated his reassuring words to David, giving him a covenant of peace and safety, and he even asked, in the form of a prayer, that God take vengeance on all of David's enemies.

20.13.0.en: Jonathan also made "David" swear by their love that he would keep his promise toward Jonathan and the people of his house, and David did this. As for the expression "he loved him as he loved his own soul", some see that it describes Jonathan's feelings and others see that it describes David's feelings toward Jonathan; combining the two opinions is better, since the two men loved each other intensely, as the following events will reveal.

20.13.1.en: It is noted that Jonathan "renewed" the covenant with David, because it was known in that time that when the rule came to a new king who was not of the offspring of the old king, the first thing the new king would do was to get rid of all the rest of the family of the former king.

20.13.2.en: It is noted here Jonathan's faith that God was with David and that he would become king after his father; therefore he asked him to care for his offspring after him.

20.13.3.en: How beautiful are the covenants of love between people... between every husband and wife, or two brothers, or two friends, that each offers love to the other, for this encourages the giving of love and its steadfastness. Love is what shatters the plots of the devil and the problems he invents every day, so that each one finds an excuse for the other and forgives him, and even has compassion on him and supports him.

20.14.s.en: (3) The plan that Jonathan made for David

20.14.0.en: Tomorrow is the new moon: that is, the king's feast at the beginning of the month.

20.14.1.en: The stone of parting: a place and a sign, meaning the place where we part and which both of us know. Jonathan proposed to David that he be absent from his father's table on the first two days of the month, the two days on which Saul gives the feast to his men, and of course everyone, Saul included, would notice David's absence. On the third day you will come to this place from which we shall now part, and its sign is this stone.

20.15.0.en: Suddenly: you come, lad, toward Jonathan to pick up the arrows.

20.15.1.en: I will go out as if strolling and hunting some animals, and I will shoot three arrows with my bow, as if I wanted to hit a target, and then I will send the lad who follows me to pick them up. I will use with him a way of speaking like a code for you to understand, David. If I say to the lad in a voice that you hear, Here are the arrows, they are near, come and take them, you will understand that matters are well and nothing will harm you, so come out of your hiding place. And he confirmed his words with an oath, As the Lord lives, that he would do what he said.

20.16.0.en: But if I say to the lad that the arrows have gone far ahead of you, so go away to pick them up and bring them, this means that you, David, are in danger and you must flee, and the Lord sends you on your way and gives you His peace.

20.17.0.en: Jonathan wanted to reassure the heart of "David", so he made the Lord a witness to his words that he would not betray him, and that the covenant he had made on himself was an everlasting covenant.

20.17.1.en: Take care to rescue everyone who is in distress, show him love and help him as far as you are able; then you will receive blessings from God and He will rescue you from every distress, and you will receive mercy on the last day.

20.18.0.en: The first of the month came and David carried out Jonathan's plan and was absent from the king's table, at which the king sat in his usual place, his face toward the entrance of the hall and his back toward the wall at the head of the table, and Abner, the commander of his army, also sat there, while Jonathan stood, perhaps to welcome the men as they entered, and David did not attend the feast.

20.19.0.en: On the first day Saul noticed David's absence but did not comment on anything; rather, he made an excuse for him and said to himself, Perhaps David did not come because of some unexpected excuse, or perhaps he was not physically clean (and this is one of the conditions for approaching and eating of the sacrifice offered to God) (Lev 7:19-21).

20.20.0.en: On the second day of the feast David's place remained empty, so Saul asked his son Jonathan about the secret of David's absence from the feast on the two days. Saul's contempt for David appears, for he did not mention him by name but said "the son of Jesse." His question was not out of love for him but to seize an opportunity to kill him.

20.21.0.en: Let me get away: allow me to be absent from the feast and go to Bethlehem.

20.21.1.en: Jonathan answered his father with the same words he had agreed with David to say (vv. 5, 6), that he went to Bethlehem, where his father offers a sacrifice for the whole clan, and that he had permitted him to go ......

20.22.0.en: Jonathan's answer kindled anger and great wrath in Saul's heart, and he could not hide his wrath but burst out, cursing his son Jonathan and describing him as disobedient and rebellious. As an insult he attributed these qualities to his mother, as if he had inherited them from her, and he told him that in choosing David as a close friend he had chosen for himself one who would be the cause of shame to him and to his whole family.

20.23.0.en: The shame of your mother's nakedness: Saul thinks that if he does not kill David, David will become king, and one of the characteristics of wicked kings is that they take the wives of the former king and make them concubines and lie with them.

20.23.1.en: Saul continued rebuking Jonathan and said that as long as "David" lived he would be the coming king, and therefore you will not inherit the kingship and the rule, and the kingdom will be lost from our family, and there is no solution for us except that you bring "David" here so that he meets his certain fate, which is death.

20.23.2.en: Thus anger and the desire for possession blind a person to the divine will, as if Saul were able by his schemes to change God's purpose and arrangement. So do not let your anger rule you, and do not make a decision while you are angry, for the wrath of man does not work the righteousness of God.

20.24.0.en: Jonathan remained faithful to his covenant of friendship and loyalty to his friend David; his father's anger did not frighten him, but he continued to defend his friend, explaining that he had done nothing wrong that he should die.

20.25.0.en: Hurled the spear: that is, turned the face of the spear toward him.

20.25.1.en: When Saul heard Jonathan's defense of David, he was angered all the more, and this time he did not use words but took the spear and tried to aim it at Jonathan to kill him, and Jonathan knew and became certain that his father's intention was to kill David and be rid of him.

20.26.0.en: Therefore Jonathan rose in anger from his father and left the place of the feast without eating anything from it, and he grieved greatly for his friend David because of the troubles that awaited him from his father, and he was also angry with his father because of his heart full of evil.

20.27.s.en: (5) The meeting of David and Jonathan and then their parting

20.27.0.en: On the morning of the third day of the month, Jonathan went out to the field agreed upon with David, with his arrows and his bow and a young lad to collect the arrows. He ordered the lad with him to start running, but Jonathan shot his arrow with force, and the arrow passed beyond the boy and fell farther than he. Perhaps he took a young lad so that he would not understand the plan agreed between him and David, who was in hiding.

20.28.0.en: Jonathan called to the boy in a loud voice so that David would hear that the arrow had gone farther than the boy, and he spoke the same words that he had agreed with David (v. 22), and then ordered the boy to go back with the arrow and bring it to him. It is noted in Jonathan's words to the lad that he gave him three commands, "Make speed, hasten, do not stay", all of which are words directed to David so that he would understand from them what he must do, that is, hasten to flee from the face of Saul, who wanted to kill him.

20.29.0.en: Of course the lad understood nothing of all these words, which were meant for David. Then Jonathan gave the lad his bow and arrows and ordered him to go back, so that he could meet his friend David alone.

20.30.0.en: David came out from the place where he was hiding and went toward Jonathan his friend and bowed before him three times, in acknowledgment of Jonathan's merit in preserving his life, and out of David's respect for Jonathan because he was the crown prince, completely forgetting that he himself was anointed by God as king. This shows his great humility and that he did not exploit his strong friendship with Jonathan. Then each embraced his friend and wept, and David wept even more than Jonathan, perhaps because his circumstances were harder than his friend's, since from now on he had to flee and hide from Saul's violence.

20.31.0.en: After a little while Jonathan spoke and told David that he must flee and go far away, and he prayed that God's safety would accompany him. He reminded him of all that they had said and sworn before God, that He is the witness of what passed between them, and how each had given a covenant of peace to his friend and to all his offspring after him. After these events Jonathan returned to the city, while David began his journey of flight.

20.31.1.en: Love urges you to warn others of the dangers that may assail them so that they may guard against them, especially the wars of Satan and everything that takes them away from God. If they listen to you, you have won their souls, and if they do not listen, you continue to pray for them until God guides them, but you must warn them, for you are responsible before God for this.
